title: Orphaned failover cascade: investigate slackback and routing state leakage
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Incident follow-up for a cross-region failover cascade that occurred on 2025-02-11 during a regional capacity degradation window. Multiple requests were escalated across region boundaries and repeatedly retried due to an interaction between the slackback cooldown mechanism and stale policy snapshot propagation. The result was amplified model variant fanout and elevated token spend plus increased user latency for ~22 minutes. This ticket captures investigation notes, identified root causes, mitigations applied during the incident, and concrete action items for long-term hardening.
impact_summary: ~22 minutes of elevated latency and 3x expected token spend for affected customers in EU-West and US-East. Several enterprise customers reported degraded throughput and a temporary SLA threshold miss. No data leakage; no unauthorized access.
timeline: 2025-02-11 10:04 UTC - First elevated error rates observed in EU-West; automated alert from routing SLOs.
2025-02-11 10:07 UTC - Router autoscaling triggered scale-up but region reported capacity imbalance; some requests were re-routed to US-East.
2025-02-11 10:09 UTC - Slackback cooldown (new mechanism) attempted to pause rapid re-tries but mis-evaluated sticky route TTL leading to orphaned handoffs.
2025-02-11 10:15 UTC - Telemetry shows repeated variant fanout loops for a subset of model families (mosaic-7b-quant variants).
2025-02-11 10:25 UTC - Mitigation: manual policy snapshot refresh and temporary decrease of retry amplification thresholds; traffic stabilised by 10:26 UTC.
2025-02-11 10:35 UTC - Incident declared resolved; post-incident analysis begun.
2025-02-12 - Full trace capture and sampling of affected requests completed; initial RCA draft created.
2025-02-18 - Engineering tabletop session to validate root cause hypotheses and evaluate permanent controls.
root_cause: Three-way interaction: (1) a delayed policy snapshot propagation to some router shards left them operating with an older fallback priority ordering; (2) the newly-deployed 'slackback' cooldown logic failed to consider sticky-route TTLs and therefore left in-flight handoffs in a half-open state (orphaned state); (3) autoscaling-induced cross-region reroutes combined with the above to cause repeated fallbacks to incompatible model variants, producing a fanout loop.
mitigations: Immediate: Force-refresh policy snapshots across all router shards and temporarily raise variant affinity TTLs to prevent immediate handoff churn.
Hotfix: Roll back the slackback cooldown change that skipped TTL checks (deployed 2025-02-11 10:22 UTC).
Monitoring: Added a temporary alert for unexpected model variant fanout ratios and for sticky-route handshake failures.
action_items: ENG-905322: Add TTL awareness to slackback cooldown logic and ensure in-flight handoffs are garbage-collected after a conservative grace window. Owner: Lucas Chen. Due: 2025-03-10.
ENG-905323: Implement end-to-end policy snapshot version checks with per-shard invariants and automated rollback if propagation exceeds 30s. Owner: Mei Rivera. Due: 2025-03-17.

ENG-905324: Introduce circuit-breaker heuristics that detect variant fanout > 1.5x baseline and short-circuit retries to a safe fallback with reduced concurrency. Owner: Tomas Alvarez. Due: 2025-03-24.
ENG-905325: Improve telemetry for 'half-open' routing states and add an explainer dashboard showing sticky-route TTL vs last-snapshot-timestamp. Owner: Priya Natarajan. Due: 2025-03-10.

ENG-905326: Run chaos tests simulating delayed policy propagation and autoscaler-induced cross-region reroutes to validate mitigations. Owner: SRE Team (lead: Jordan Blake). Estimate: 3 days. Due: 2025-03-31.

ENG-905327: Update runbook and on-call playbook: include immediate steps to refresh policy snapshots, temporarily reduce retry multipliers, and how to safely roll back slackback changes. Owner: Incident Response (lead: Aisha Kapoor). Due: 2025-03-05.

ENG-905328: Perform a cost-analysis report for token-spend amplification during cascading reroutes and propose rate-limits or budget throttles for third-party customers. Owner: Platform Economics (lead: Ravi Singh). Due: 2025-03-20.
notes: This incident exposed a subtle correctness gap in a recently shipped cooldown optimization (slackback). Prior code paths implicitly relied on synchronous snapshot propagation; the optimization assumed low snapshot latency and lacked defensive checks.
Recommend treating 'policy snapshot age' as a first-class signal in routing decisions rather than as background telemetry.
Customer success already contacted top two impacted customers and provided a brief incident summary; follow-up scheduled once action items complete.
